arxiv-2104-03395.title: Bayesian estimation of dynamic weights in Gaussian mixture models
arxiv-2104-03395.creator: Michel H. Montoril a ; Leandro T. Correia b and Helio S. Migon c
arxiv-2104-03395.description: Abstract This paper proposes a generalization of Gaussian mixture models, where the mixture weight is allowed to behave as an unknown function of time. This model is capable of successfully capturing the features of the data, as demonstrated by simulated and real datasets. It can be useful in studies such as clustering, change-point and process control.

arxiv-2104-04703.title: Echo Chambers: Voter-to-Voter Communication and Political Competition This paper is based on a chapter of my PhD dissertation at the University of Warwick. I am grateful to Mirko Draca, Walter Ferrarese, Carlo Perroni, Herakles Polemarchakis, Simone Tonin. I am also grateful to seminar participants
arxiv-2104-04703.creator: Monica A. Giovanniello
arxiv-2104-04703.description: Abstract Abstract I study how strategic communication among voters shapes both political outcomes and parties’ advertising strategies in a model of informative campaign advertising. Two main results are derived. First, echo chambers arise endogenously. Surprisingly, small ideological distance between voters is not sufficient to guarantee that a chamber is created, biases’ direction plays a crucial role.

arxiv-2108-06392.title: Preserving operators on semiprime f f -algebras
arxiv-2108-06392.creator: Jaber Jamel, Khalfaoui ADNEN
arxiv-2108-06392.description: Abstract It is an open problem whether a separating operator acting between semiprime f f -algebras is a weighted composition operator ( [ 1 , problem 2.6] ). We prove that the answer is positive if and only if the separating operator is almost contractive. As a consequence, we can generalized and strengthen some well-known results on separating operators.

arxiv-2112-02274.title: Self-supervised Graph Learning for Occasional Group Recommendation
arxiv-2112-02274.creator: Bowen Hao, Hongzhi Yin, Cuiping Li, Hong Chen
arxiv-2112-02274.description: Abstract As an important branch in Recommender System, occasional group recommendation has received more and more attention. In this scenario, each occasional group (cold-start group) has no or few historical interacted items. As each occasional group has extremely sparse interactions with items, traditional group recommendation methods can not learn high-quality group representations.

arxiv-2202-13535.title: Maximising Wrenches for Kinematically Redundant Systems with Experiments on UVMS
arxiv-2202-13535.creator: Wilhelm J. Marais, Stefan B. Williams, Oscar Pizarro
arxiv-2202-13535.description: Abstract This paper presents methods for finding optimal configurations and actuator forces/torques to maximise contact wrenches in a desired direction for Underwater Vehicles Manipulator Systems (UVMS). The wrench maximisation problem is formulated as a linear programming problem, and the optimal configuration is solved as a bi-level optimisation in the parameterised redundancy space.

arxiv-2211-11159.title: Directed Acyclic Graph Factorization Machines for CTR Prediction via Knowledge Distillation Conference: Proceedings of the Sixteenth ACM International Conference on Web Search and Data Mining; February 27-March 3, 2023; Singapore, Singapore Proceedings of the Sixteenth ACM International Conference o
arxiv-2211-11159.creator: Zhen Tian, Ting Bai ∗‡, Zibin Zhang Zhiyuan Xu, Kangyi Lin, Ji-Rong Wen †, Wayne Xin Zhao †
arxiv-2211-11159.description: A 2022 arXiv research paper by Zhen Tian, Ting Bai ∗‡, Zibin Zhang Zhiyuan Xu, Kangyi Lin, Ji-Rong Wen †, Wayne Xin Zhao †. With the growth of high-dimensional sparse data in web-scale recommender systems, the computational cost to learn high-order feature interaction in CTR prediction task largely increases, which limits the use of high-order interaction models in real industrial applications. Some recent knowledge distillation based methods transfer knowledge from complex teacher models to shallow student models for accelerating the online model inference.

arxiv-2310-11731.title: Action-Quantized Offline Reinforcement Learning for Robotic Skill Learning
arxiv-2310-11731.creator: Jianlan Luo Perry Dong Jeffrey Wu Aviral Kumar Xinyang Geng Sergey Levine
arxiv-2310-11731.description: Abstract The offline reinforcement learning (RL) paradigm provides a general recipe to convert static behavior datasets into policies that can perform better than the policy that collected the data. While policy constraints, conservatism, and other methods for mitigating distributional shifts have made offline reinforcement learning more effective, the continuous action setting often necessitates various approximations for applying these techniques.

arxiv-2405-05054.title: Beam-induced backgrounds measured in the ATLAS detector during local gas injection into the LHC beam vacuum
arxiv-2405-05054.description: Abstract Inelastic beam-gas collisions at the Large Hadron Collider (LHC), within a few hundred metres of the ATLAS experiment, are known to give the dominant contribution to beam backgrounds. These are monitored by ATLAS with a dedicated Beam Conditions Monitor (BCM) and with the rate of fake jets in the calorimeters.

arxiv-2406-11074.title: Cusps of caustics by reflection in ellipses
arxiv-2406-11074.creator: Gil Bor, Mark Spivakovsky, Serge Tabachnikov
arxiv-2406-11074.description: A 2024 arXiv research paper by Gil Bor, Mark Spivakovsky, Serge Tabachnikov. This paper is concerned with the billiard version of Jacobi’s last geometric statement and its generalizations. Given a non-focal point O O inside an elliptic billiard table, one considers the family of rays emanating from O O and the caustic Γ n \Gamma_{n} of the reflected family after n n reflections off the ellipse, for each positive integer n n .

arxiv-2503-17407.title: A Comprehensive Survey on Long Context Language Modeling
arxiv-2503-17407.creator: Jiaheng Liu ∗,† , Dawei Zhu ∗,† , Zhiqi Bai ⋆ , Yancheng He ⋆ , Huanxuan Liao ⋆ , Haoran Que ⋆ , Zekun Wang ⋆ , Chenchen Zhang ⋆ , Ge Zhang ⋆ , Jiebin Zhang ⋆ , Yuanxing Zhang ⋆ , Zhuo Chen, Hangyu Guo, Shilong Li, Ziqiang Liu, Yong Shan, Yifan Song, Jiayi Tian, Wenhao Wu, Zhejian Zhou, Ruijie Zhu,
arxiv-2503-17407.description: Abstract Efficient processing of long contexts has been a persistent pursuit in Natural Language Processing. With the growing number of long documents, dialogues, and other textual data, it is important to develop Long Context Language Models (LCLMs) that can process and analyze extensive inputs in an effective and efficient way.

arxiv-2504-13602.title: A new thermodynamic function for binary mixtures: the co-molar volume
arxiv-2504-13602.creator: Kristian Polanco Olsen, Bjørn Hafskjold, Anders Lervik, Alex Hansen
arxiv-2504-13602.description: Abstract We have developed a new theory relating partial molar volumes of binary mixtures to the specific (Voronoi) volumes. A simple relation gives new insight into the physical meaning of partial molar volumes in terms of the actual volumes occupied by the molecules. Partial molar quantities are defined through the use of the Euler theorem for homogeneous functions.

arxiv-2505-07956.title: Symbolic Regression with Multimodal Large Language Models and Kolmogorov–Arnold Networks
arxiv-2505-07956.description: Abstract We present a novel approach to symbolic regression using vision-capable large language models (LLMs) and the ideas behind Google DeepMind’s Funsearch . The LLM is given a plot of a univariate function and tasked with proposing an ansatz for that function.

arxiv-2510-03811.title: Curriculum-Augmented GFlowNets For mRNA Sequence Generation
arxiv-2510-03811.creator: Aya Laajil, Abduragim Shtanchaev, Sajan Muhammad, Eric Moulines, Salem Lahlou
arxiv-2510-03811.description: Abstract Designing mRNA sequences is a major challenge in developing next-generation therapeutics, since it involves exploring a vast space of possible nucleotide combinations while optimizing sequence properties like stability, translation efficiency, and protein expression. While Generative Flow Networks are promising for this task, their training is hindered by sparse, long-horizon rewards and multi-objective trade-offs.

pmc-12361858.title: Diagnostic accuracy differences in detecting wound maceration between humans and artificial intelligence: the role of human expertise revisited
pmc-12361858.creator: Florian Kücking, Ursula H Hübner, Dorothee Busch
pmc-12361858.description: ObjectiveThis study aims to compare the diagnostic abilities of humans in wound image assessment with those of an AI-based model, examine how “expertise” affects clinicians’ diagnostic performance, and investigate the heterogeneity in clinical judgments.Materials and MethodsA total of 481 healthcare professionals completed a diagnostic task involving 30 chronic wound images with and without maceration.

pmc-13148261.title: Combined Occipital Nerve and Sphenopalatine Ganglion Neuromodulation for Refractory Craniofacial Pain with Trigeminal Autonomic Features: A 12-Year Follow-Up (Case Report)
pmc-13148261.creator: Vadim Tashlykov, Ruth Gur, Gabriel Ricardo Lichtenstein, Itay Goor-Aryeh, Evgeni Brotfain
pmc-13148261.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). Craniofacial complex regional pain syndrome (CRPS) is a rare, diagnostically challenging condition characterized by sympathetically maintained pain, allodynia, and autonomic features in the craniofacial region. Its overlap with trigeminal autonomic cephalalgias (TACs) creates significant diagnostic complexity. We report the case of a 41-year-old male with a 12-year history of severe right-sided hemicranial and facial pain with prominent autonomic features (facial edema, ptosis, lacrimation, allodynia) following plastic surgery in occipital area, in a patient with a prior history of CRPS.

pmc-13277639.title: Thermally Bistable Stiff Stilbene Photoswitches and Polymer Applications
pmc-13277639.creator: Keiichi Imato
pmc-13277639.description: Photoresponsive molecular switches (photoswitches) enable reversible control of molecular structures and properties using light, offering powerful opportunities for functional materials. However, their practical use in polymeric systems has long been constrained by thermal instability, which also hampers mechanistic understanding and precise control.

pmc-13595494.title: Out of Sight, Out of Mind: Shedding Light on Two Blind Spots in Harm Reduction Discourse
pmc-13595494.creator: Simon Clay, Wayne Hall
pmc-13595494.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). Harm reduction policies aim to reduce drug‐related harms. This has historically involved providing tailored health services to people who use drugs to do so more safely. Social justice is another defining element of harm reduction. This component aims to reduce drug‐related stigma and minimise the social harms experienced by people who use drugs by advocating for the decriminalisation of the possession of illicit drugs.

pmc-13644581.title: 3D reconstruction of a model phytophagous mite at nano-resolution reveals a peculiar ingestion and digestion system and structural adaptation for a tiny animal
pmc-13644581.creator: Jian-Sheng Guo, Dan-Ting Li, Guan Wang, Xin-Qiu Wang, Bernard Moussian, Chuan-Xi Zhang
pmc-13644581.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2025). The fine structure of the globally distributed phytophagous mite, Tetranychus urticae, has been elucidated using serial block-face scanning electron microscopy (SBF-SEM) combined with 3D reconstruction. The reconstructed models reveal previously unknown internal adaptations tailored to its unique lifestyle. These include a specialized food ingestion structure to facilitate effective cell-sucking, a semi-closed-loop tracheal system optimized for efficient oxygen diffusion in a minute organism, and a pair of well-developed silk glands utilized for water repellency, defense and dispersion.
